question: After I opt in to a limited-time higher-earn offer on my card, how will the extra rewards appear on my statement, and when might they show up later than the purchases?
answer: On your statement, you'll see your rewards totaled as points in the Rewards Summary section. Your standard cash back will appear as it normally does. Your bonus cash back will be broken out separately into categories with a description of "Bonus from Q2 5% category." And if you activate after the quarter has started, you will still get your bonus cash back on applicable purchases made since April 1, 2026. It will show as "Retro(active) Q2 5% cat(egory) bonus." In most cases, once you activate your 5% cash back in quarterly bonus categories, you’ll see your rewards on the same statement you see your purchases. However, if your purchase was made within 1-2 weeks before your statement closing date, you may see your corresponding rewards on your next statement.

### Seeing your 5% cash back in quarterly bonus categories
Activate to earn 5% cash back from April 1, 2026 through June 30, 2026 on Amazon, Chase Travel℠, and Feeding America® on up to $1,500 in total combined purchases. That means for Amazon and Feeding America® you earn 4% cash back in addition to your 1% standard cash back, adding up to a total of 5% cash back.
This quarter, you earn more on bonus categories by stacking with your standard category earn. For Chase Travel purchases, you will earn 9% cash back (5% Chase Travel cash back + 4% bonus category cash back).
On your statement, you'll see your rewards totaled as points in the Rewards Summary section. Your standard cash back will appear as it normally does. Your bonus cash back will be broken out separately into categories with a description of "Bonus from Q2 5% category." And if you activate after the quarter has started, you will still get your bonus cash back on applicable purchases made since April 1, 2026. It will show as "Retro(active) Q2 5% cat(egory) bonus."
In most cases, once you activate your 5% cash back in quarterly bonus categories, you’ll see your rewards on the same statement you see your purchases. However, if your purchase was made within 1-2 weeks before your statement closing date, you may see your corresponding rewards on your next statement.

question: If someone wants to try buying a home again after previously falling far behind on payments for a home they already financed, and they’re worried because their number used by lenders is currently too low, what other factors might a lender still look at besides that number, and what long-lasting credit-report consequence from the earlier home loss could continue hurting them?
answer: Credit score is not the only factor mortgage providers review—your down payment and debt-to-income (DTI) ratio are also considered. If you've taken out a mortgage and miss your payments for an extensive period of time, your home could be foreclosed. Having a foreclosure on your report will be seen as a derogatory mark. This can remain on your report for up to 7 years and can harm your credit score further.

## What if your credit score doesn’t meet the FHA loan requirements?
If your credit score falls below an FHA loan requirement, you could continue on your journey toward homeownership. Credit score is not the only factor mortgage providers review—your down payment and debt-to-income (DTI) ratio are also considered. Lenders review potential borrowers differently but generally look at a range of financial factors.

reference_chunks.content:
### Defaulting on a mortgage loan
A mortgage is a type of loan you take out when you are looking to buy a home. It is a type of secured loan, meaning that there are assets involved. If you've taken out a mortgage and miss your payments for an extensive period of time, you could face some unfortunate consequences. Your home could be foreclosed, meaning the lender can repossess your home.
Defaulting on a mortgage can result in some serious damage to your credit score. In addition to the late payments harming your payment history, which is a major factor in determining your score, having a foreclosure on your report will be seen as a derogatory mark. This can remain on your report for up to 7 years and can harm your credit score further.
